name: Figma & design systems
blurb: Figma MCP, tokens and variables, code-Figma sync and drift, component and screen-reader specs, hand-off, design-to-code and audits.
searches: Figma MCP use_figma agent skill new
design tokens Figma variables sync skill DTCG Style Dictionary
component spec documentation agent skill Figma accessibility
design system audit skill Figma drift parity
Figma design to code skill Claude Code Connect

tests.prompt: Export the variables from our Figma file (https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Brand-Library) into Tailwind v4 and CSS for our Next.js app. We have Light and Dark modes.
tests.good: Parses the file key; notes get_variable_defs is default-mode only and the REST Variables API is Enterprise-only; runs read-variables.js via use_figma (read-only), then convert-tokens.mjs to tailwind-v4 and css-vars with both modes; reports converter warnings; normalises opacity 0-100 to 0-1 and rounds float noise; keeps semantic tokens as var() references with a dark block; checks text/background contrast in both modes; lands it as a reviewable diff, never hand-editing generated files; states who owns the tokens.

tests.prompt: Write a screen reader spec for our text field component (label, input, helper text, error message, and a clear button that appears when there's text).
tests.good: Runs a merge analysis first: label, helper and error merge into the input; clear button is a conditional second stop; error is a live region, not a stop. Gives a focus order section, collapses states with identical semantics, keeps error and disabled separate, and provides VoiceOver, TalkBack and ARIA tables per stop (label/value/traits/hint; content/role/state; native input with label, aria-describedby, aria-invalid) each with Do NOT rows (no double-read label, placeholder not the name, clear icon labelled). States the disabled policy.

tests.prompt: Audit our Figma component library against the React components in packages/ui and tell me what's out of sync. Then fix it.
tests.good: Agrees scope and files and respects the seat's call limits; runs lint-design.js (design-system and wcag rules) per page and check-parity.js with a CODE_SPEC per key component; searches code for raw colours and arbitrary values; reports findings with node ids or file paths, severity and fix, grouped by root cause, with a parity score and probable renames; proposes fixes and asks before any Figma write or library publish; re-runs checks and shows before and after.

tests.prompt: Turn the checkout frame in our Figma file (https://www.figma.com/design/XyZ789/Checkout?node-id=12-34) into React components in our Next.js + shadcn/ui app, using our existing tokens. Add tests that catch it when the build drifts from the design.
tests.good: States a short plan first: the bridge here (figma-mcp.md: get_metadata, then targeted reads; token-sync-and-drift.md; design-to-code.md: reuse existing components and map every value to a token, gaps listed), the build through frontend-ui-design (components-and-states.md and react-shadcn-tailwind.md: every field and button state, including loading, error and disabled), the tests through testing-qa (playwright-e2e.md: toHaveScreenshot at a fixed viewport with dynamic regions masked, role-based locators for the pay flow). Runs check-parity.js on key components; compares renders at mobile and desktop; checks the Done means of all three crafts and says what wasn't verified.

tests.prompt: We keep our component library in Storybook and design in Figma. Set up Storybook's MCP so you can see our real components, then use it to build the new Settings page from this Figma frame https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/App?node-id=412-905 using only components we already have, and write stories for anything new you add.
tests.good: Installs the Storybook MCP addon (`npx storybook add @storybook/addon-mcp`) and registers it on the dev server's /mcp endpoint, asking before installing or changing config. Reads the frame with the Figma MCP (file key and node 412:905 parsed from the URL, `get_design_context` per section, `get_variable_defs`) rather than guessing from a screenshot. Uses docs-list and docs-show to find existing components and their props before writing any new one, and reports which frame parts mapped to which components. Maps Figma variables to the project's existing tokens and flags values with no token instead of hardcoding. Writes stories for new components covering default, hover, focus, disabled and error states, then runs the Storybook test-run tool or the project's tests and shows the result. Checks the page at mobile and desktop widths against the frame, and does not touch the Figma file, publish or push without asking.

tools.name: Figma
tools.why: Primary design tool of 82.3% of designers in the UX Tools survey (46:1 over Sketch); official remote MCP server with canvas writes, Dev Mode, Variables and a Plugin API.

tools.name: Storybook
tools.why: Default component workshop and living docs for React, Vue, Angular and Svelte design systems (Design Systems Report 2025 round-ups name Figma plus Storybook as the dominant pair); has an official MCP addon with docs-list, docs-show and test-run.

tools.name: Style Dictionary
tools.why: The standard token build tool (4.8k GitHub stars, Apache-2.0); v4 reads DTCG directly; named in every 2025-26 design-system tool round-up.

tools.name: Tokens Studio
tools.why: Most installed design-system plugin in Figma (about 264k users per the dupple round-up); stores tokens as JSON in git and feeds Style Dictionary via sd-transforms.

tools.name: W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) format
tools.why: Vendor-neutral token interchange format supported by Figma variables export, Style Dictionary v4, Penpot and Tokens Studio.

tools.name: Tailwind CSS v4
tools.why: Default styling target for generated front ends (97k GitHub stars); v4 puts tokens in CSS `@theme`, which is where Figma variables land.

tools.name: Figma Make
tools.why: UX Tools Spring 2026 survey (1,478 designers) lists Figma Make among the weekly AI tools next to Claude and Claude Code; the Figma MCP server exposes Make file resources.

tools.name: Sketch
tools.why: Second-largest UI design app (about 7% against Figma's 82% in 2026 round-ups of the UX Tools survey) with a built-in local MCP server (run_code, get_layer_tree_summary, get_screenshot, get_symbol_overrides).

tools.name: Penpot
tools.why: Only production-grade open-source design tool, over 500k active users in 2026 round-ups; has a remote MCP (MCP key) and a local `npx @penpot/mcp@stable` server.

tools.name: Figma Code Connect
tools.why: Figma's official way to map design-system components to real code so Dev Mode and MCP output reuse them; used by teams such as Coinbase, JustEatTakeaway and Chromium in public repos.

tools.name: Framer
tools.why: Leading designer-friendly site builder (4.5/5 satisfaction in the UX Tools survey); native Claude Code connection through `npx @framer/agent setup` with canvas, components and CMS access.

tools.name: zeroheight
tools.why: Most-cited documentation platform for design systems in the 2025-26 tool round-ups; publishes its own Design Systems Report and a remote MCP that gives coding agents live guidelines.

tools.name: Supernova
tools.why: Design-system platform that serves tokens, components and docs over a hosted MCP (https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp) with skills bundled and no call limits on any plan.

tools.name: Figma Console MCP
tools.why: 2.4k stars (MIT); community MCP with Desktop Bridge plugin for variables, lint, parity and comments; the base of this craft's scripts.

tools.name: Framelink Figma MCP
tools.why: 15.9k stars (MIT), the most starred community Figma MCP and used with Cursor for one-shot design-to-code; reads Figma via the REST API with a personal access token.

tools.name: Stark
tools.why: Most-used accessibility plugin for Figma (568k+ users per 2026 plugin round-ups; Stark cites 40k+ paying-team users at 28k companies) with contrast, focus order, alt-text, landmarks and touch-target checks; now in Claude's connector directory, scanning Figma files, URLs, code and Storybook.

tools.name: Zeplin
tools.why: Named with Figma Dev Mode and Anima as the three most adopted hand-off tools in 2026 round-ups; imports from Figma, Sketch and XD, and has an official MCP server (@zeplin/mcp-server, MIT) exposing screen and component specs, assets, annotations and tokens.

tools.name: Anima
tools.why: One of the top Figma-to-code plugins in 2026 round-ups and listed among the three most adopted hand-off tools; official remote MCP (https://public-api.animaapp.com/v1/mcp, OAuth) turns Figma frames into stack-specific code with assets and snapshots.

tools.name: Builder.io Visual Copilot
tools.why: Figma-to-code plugin claiming 1.25M+ designers and developers (vendor figure); maps Figma components to code components and generates React, Vue, Svelte, Angular or HTML through `npx @builder.io/dev-tools`.
